--- PART 1/3 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "GENERAL COOPERATION ADVICE. This is general guidance, not a measurement or diagnosis of this parent." and "Use these general suggestions while pursuing the stated tournament objective."
STRATEGY: Parent is a mostly TFT strategy with early forgiveness and later retaliation. The trace simulates the parent and the listed population strategies, analyzing payoffs and exploitability. It proposes changes such as always defecting on the last round, probing near the end, and exploiting opponents whose cooperation-rate thresholds allow occasional defections.

--- PART 2/3 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "So overall, many opponents are exploitable by maintaining a low defection rate (e.g., 10-15%) and defecting on those rounds to get 5 instead of 3."
STRATEGY: The parent is a TFT-with-thresholds strategy that retaliates when opponent defection rates exceed thresholds (e.g., 15%). The trace simulates many slots (Generous TFT, TFT variants, forgiving strategies) and designs an adaptive strategy that probes at round 10, defects periodically against forgiving opponents while keeping defection rate below ~10%, and defects on the last round.

--- PART 3/3 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "This is similar to the parent strategy: it forgives early if opp_defects <= n//10. We can use a similar threshold."
STRATEGY: Parent is a forgiving TFT-like strategy that forgives early if opponent defections are low. The trace simulates a revised strategy with proactive scheduled defections plus forgiving TFT after retaliation. It changes the schedule, retaliation detection, early-defection handling, and forgiveness thresholds.
